comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parallel run recognized the 58 requirement slugs from the prompt and attempted broad requirement coverage through delegated slug work.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial run received the same prompt and requirement list, and worked through the same 58 slugs across resumed serial rounds.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The required scope was the same; the material difference was not task recognition but how the visualmap collision fix and shared workspace were handled.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parent decomposed the whole task into one 58-item AgentSwarm, assigning one slug per subagent in a single shared /workspace.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial control disabled Agent and AgentSwarm, with protocol validation showing no delegation or subagents.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel maximized breadth and per-slug ownership; serial kept ownership in one main actor and avoided cross-agent write coordination.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The child brief gave each agent a slug and shared workflow rules, but it did not provide isolated repository state or private git-index boundaries.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial actor carried context forward in the same session/workspace without needing inter-agent handoffs or cross-agent contracts.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No missing task fact explains the score delta; the important boundary is workspace/interface isolation between writers, not a child brief omission.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: For visualmap-handle-label-collision, parallel changed horizontal label verticalAlign based on handleThumb and did not add the y-axis minimum-size offset checked by the unit test.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial computed align from shapes.mainGroup and adjusted textPoint[1] by minimumOffset for horizontal visualMaps, matching the tested geometry.
comparison_dimensions.difference: This ordinary implementation difference explains the testcase-level delta: parallel failed 20249 while serial passed it.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The first parallel swarm returned 52 completed and 6 aborted children, then later rounds continued from remaining work and mixed child reports.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial run proceeded through resumed rounds without child result joins; the final agent prompt completed successfully before evaluation.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had a child-result aggregation and recovery lifecycle; serial had a single actor lifecycle, so no child join or result adoption boundary was needed.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel subagents repeatedly reported shared-index and shared-worktree contamination, including foreign files in commits and wrong commit provenance.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial status shows no delegation or subagents, so there was no multi-agent shared-index integration surface.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The retained parallel pattern is the shared workspace write boundary; serial avoided that class of instability.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Official post-test completed 51 tests with 47 passes and failed 20030, 20249, 20398, and 20484.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Official post-test completed the same 51 tests with 48 passes, passing 20249 and failing only 20030, 20398, and 20484.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both officially failed, but the closest quality evidence shows serial one testcase ahead because of visualmap-handle-label-collision.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Round 1 timed out after a broad swarm and the overall parallel adapter reported very high tool and token use across two rounds.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial control used three sequential rounds and the final prompt completed without child-agent budget or swarm-retry pressure.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel spent budget managing breadth and contaminated shared state; serial spent budget on sequential implementation and cleanup.

outcome_analysis.explanation: The current official status evaluation resolves the pair as both_fail, not an official pass/fail discordance. The closest testcase evidence is still materially different: parallel passed 47/51 and serial passed 48/51. The extra parallel failure is 20249. In the visualmap patch, parallel changed horizontal handle label verticalAlign from the handle thumb, while serial added the minimumOffset y-position adjustment for horizontal size visualMaps, so serial satisfied that testcase. The retained concurrency pattern is adverse process evidence about shared workspace provenance, but it is not proved to be the direct cause of the 20249 implementation miss.
parallel_contributors: Parallel used a 58-child AgentSwarm in one shared workspace.
Parallel's visualmap implementation omitted the tested horizontal y-offset.
Parallel shared-index/write contamination made patch and commit provenance unreliable.
serial_contributors: Serial avoided delegation and shared-index contention.
Serial implemented the visualmap horizontal minimumOffset behavior and passed 20249.
ordinary_implementation_differences: The 20249 delta is an ordinary implementation difference in ContinuousView.ts rather than a proven concurrency root cause.
Both runs shared failed testcases 20030, 20398, and 20484.
evaluator_effects: The resolver returns passed, total, and rate as null because status.json lacks recognized aggregate quality fields; post-test logs provide the closest testcase counts.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: supported comparative explanation with one retained adverse parallel coordination pattern, not an exclusive root cause for the official failure

The parent launched one 58-item AgentSwarm in one /workspace and the child reports show live shared git index, worktree, stash, and history contamination: foreign files were swept into commits, changes were orphaned or restored, and marker or regenerated diffs were needed to recover provenance. The serial control had no delegation or subagents and produced its changes sequentially. Corrective boundary: give each child an isolated worktree/private index and merge reviewed patches explicitly.
